except.note: Without the keyring extra or a usable OS keyring the token is in a 0600 file; store_status() reports keyring-unavailable and supports() reports dependency (P1b-10).

core.store.note: keyring is an optional extra; without it the token is in a 0600 file and store_status() reports keyring-unavailable.

core.copy.note: polaris_key.copy serves copy_generated.py (from copy.en.json): message()/title() read the error-code, then gate, then activation table; activation_message()/activation_title() and describe_error() read typed activation results from the activation table only; unknown codes read COPY_FALLBACK naming the code; {name} placeholders fill or drop; register_locale('en', ...) is the host override layer. The hand-kept EN table is gone. tests/test_copy.py checks every table against copy.en.json.

core.backend.note: client.backend (polaris_key.backend): headers(), httpx_auth() (sync and async) and requests_auth() send X-PKey-License and X-PKey-Device only; backend.origins (exact, HTTPS except loopback) is checked on the request and, for requests, on every redirect hop; the freshness pre-sync, one shared concurrent sync, one retry on license_stale/license_invalid, and not_entitled/sign_in_required raised typed. tests/test_backend.py replays backend-matrix.json's client rows.

core.devicekeys.note: polaris_key.devices.keys (create_device_key_store) over cryptography: a 0600 file in a 0700 state directory, fcntl.flock / msvcrt.locking, atomic os.replace; an unreadable record is an error that only wipe() resets; client.devices.register_keys sends PUT /devices/keys. The pkey-proof/1 signer and verifier are polaris_key.core.device_keys / device_proof. tests/test_device_keys.py, tests/test_device_proof_conformance.py.

license.manage.note: PX-W8: the device-limit result exposes manageUrl (validated), plus the return and key helpers.

config.mirror.note: The Python mirror is rendered by tools/gen-mirrors.ts.

telemetry.updates.note: core/update_journal.py UpdateJournal: at most 16 queued events ride each devices/report in updates, oldest first, dropped once a 200 delivers them.

devices.attest.note: P6-02: a CPython process has no platform attestation service; its devices stay at the basic trust level.

identity.oidc.note: Browser redirect sign-in waits on the native redirect-token route (I-15, SDK parity pass wire item W4). Until then identity.sign_in.start() answers a device-code session whose reopen() opens verification_uri_complete in the system browser and whose wait() polls /identity/auth/device/poll (identity.devicecode); the old /identity/auth/poll is retired and the Worker no longer serves it.

identity.devicelabel.note: PX-W13: normalize_device_label (polaris_key.core.device_label), the device_name option and platform.node() without .local/.lan/.home by default, on sign_in.start, activate_with_key and register; SignInSession.device_name is the Worker's echo.

identity.redirect.web.note: I-10a.17: identity.sign_in.start(channel="redirect", redirect_uri=...) builds the S256 authorize URL from discovery (identity/redirect.py, hashlib) for a browser the host opens; session.complete(callback_url) checks the redirect URI, state and iss before anything is sent, then redeems the code at discovery's token endpoint (form body, product origin only). Single use; a refusal is a SignInError carrying retry_after_seconds and never wipes the token. Loopback, scheme and claimed-HTTPS redirects are I-15's.

identity.choice.note: I-10a.17: identity.choice.licenses/devices/complete/cancel over the endpoints discovery names (typed service-unavailable N/A otherwise), no bearer (but for keep, which sends the device token: holders-add-to-account), the grant never in an error; a Worker refusal is a ChoiceRefused result (retry_after_seconds, manage_url, sign_in_url, key_entries, the fresh view); keep completes attachable; a redirect choose answer settles as the choice outcome only when the session asked for license_choice="app". The three choice-* and two redirect-web-choose* transcripts are replayed.

identity.exchange.note: No OS account to take a platform identity from (I-13); Python signs in by loopback or device code.

identity.gamecenter.note: Game Center exists only on Apple platforms.

identity.pgs.note: Play Games runs only on Android.

identity.link.note: No OS account to offer a link from (I-43).

identity.keyentry.note: I-10a: ActivationOk.key_entries, ActivationKeyEntryLimit(manage_url, key_entries) and ActivationLicenseOwned(sign_in_url); no wipe, no retry.

release.record.note: core/release_record.py verify_release_record (hash before signature, pinned release keys only, never a product key); client.update.release_record() and decide() fetch by hash and keep the releaseRecords slice while a committed feed pins it.

release.fetch.note: client.release.fetch(target, to=…): discovery's build template, device bearer and metadata headers, Range/If-Range resume, size and SHA-256 checked before the file appears.

update.feed.note: core/feed.py verify_feed with floors keyed by the canonical channel; client.update.feed() and decide() fetch, verify and commit the feeds cache slice, re-verified on load.

update.feeds.note: client.update.feed_url(kind) over discovery's update.endpoints (aliases canonicalised, values percent-encoded, velopack without a channel is the UpdateManager directory); tests/test_feed_url_matrix.py drives every feed-url-matrix.json row.

update.decide.note: core/decide.py decide_update over core/check.py run_update_check; client.update.decide() returns the UpdateCheck at the effective clock. The outlet is the host's UpdateClientOptions.outlet, else the in-process detection result (P3-11) over the stamp.

update.content.note: core/decide.py decide_update with content (feed_content, select_pack_rows, prestage, the content blocks and boot required for revoked required content); client.update.decide() builds content from the content stamp, the pack state, the variant preferences and the stored revocations (run_update_check steps 10-14).

update.driver.note: update/drivers.py: client.update.install(decision) over VelopackDriver (the velopack package's UpdateManager on discovery's Velopack feed; unsupported dependency without it), SelfReplaceDriver (a frozen single-file executable replaced with the release.fetch-verified build, the old one kept for the boot guard's rollback) and StoreLinkDriver (a store decision's listing); each records update_downloaded and update_applied. tests/test_drivers.py.

update.bootguard.note: update/bootguard.py BootGuard: update.mark_boot_attempt() at launch (client.boot() calls it) and update.confirm_boot() once healthy (boot() confirms per stage-matrix.json's bootConfirmation), slots in the state directory; after maxFailedBoots unconfirmed launches it rolls back through the install driver when one can (update_reverted, boot_rolled_back), otherwise reports boot_rolled_back with code no-previous once. tests/test_boot.py drives the guardCases.

outlet.detect.note: core/detection.py detect_outlet over update/outlet.py read_outlet_signals (environment, sys.executable and script path conventions, product-named markers, GetCurrentPackageFamilyName through ctypes); the update client detects when the host names no outlet. PEP 376 INSTALLER names no v4 signal and is not read.

packs.record.note: core.release_record verify_release_record with pin.kind (pack records fetched by the content stamp's pin, app content and builds[].embeds claims) and update.packs.verify_marker for embedded baselines; test_conformance drives every packRecordCases and markerCases vector, test_content_conformance the stampCases.

packs.revoke.note: core/release_record.py verify_revocation and newer_revocation; the PackEngine keeps verified revocations in the sibling revocations.json (revocationsStored, relearn, 256 targets) and refuses revoked mounts with pack-revoked.

packs.delegation.note: core/release_record.py verify_release_record (the delegated path, steps 13 and 16), verify_delegation, record_revoked and update/packs/dataonly.py data_only_refusal; the PackEngine fetches and caches delegations, refuses non-data-only delegated installs with pack-not-data-only, stores the install's delegation and refuses releases under a revoked delegation (pack-revoked, detail delegation); test_delegation_conformance drives every delegationCases and dataOnlyCases vector.

packs.plan.note: update.packs plan, select_variant and plan_target; every plan-matrix.json row, variant case and target case in test_plan_matrix.

packs.index.files.note: update.packs parse_files_index, check_paths and tree_digest; filesIndexCases under compression.zstd (3.14+) and zstandard.

packs.index.chunks.note: update.packs parse_chunk_index and parse_chunk_index_bytes (u64 from two u32 reads, saturated at 2^53); chunkIndexCases under compression.zstd (3.14+) and zstandard. Seed indexes are kept under <packs root>/index/<sha256> and re-verified on every use.

packs.apply.full.note: update.packs apply_full (streamed through decode_stream); applyCases under every backend the interpreter has.

packs.apply.file.note: update.packs apply_file with the type-neutral container rebuild; applyCases under every backend.

packs.apply.chunk.note: update.packs apply_chunk over seeds from every installed and embedded container (across packs), one bounded Range request per run with If-Range and Accept-Encoding: identity through chunk_range_fetch (exact Content-Range and ETag, never multi-range); a run journal resumes an interrupted install and a refused range falls back to the next strategy. applyCases under every backend the interpreter has.

packs.apply.delta.note: compression.zstd's ZstdDict(base, is_raw=True).as_prefix on 3.14+, zstandard's DICT_TYPE_RAWCONTENT below (a hard dependency there), window_log_max always set; the window check runs in the applier whatever the decoder, and a start-up probe gates zstd-patch-from.

packs.delta.feed.note: feed_content reads the feed's deltas menu (both caps, both uniqueness rules, a non-payload entry dropped alone), with_feed_deltas merges it into the selected container variant before plan_target, and PackEngine tries at most one feed-offered delta per install (fallback on a failed fetch or any delta verdict), journalling it as feedDelta for resume; UpdateClient wires feed_deltas to the committed feed (fresh or stale).

packs.state.note: update.packs PackEngine and the install-state machine over DirPackStorage in the platform data directory: journal, resume with Range/If-Range, atomic pointer swap with fsync, confirm, rollback, GC roots, a torn state.json held aside, an unreadable one refused, embedded baselines; packSetId on devices/report.

packs.handlers.note: client.update.packs.register_handler; files.tree (hot: versioned directory plus pointer swap), data.json and l10n.table built in; a handler's optional check(staged) runs over every newly staged payload before the state commit (pack-type-check-failed with detail and path), and a reads_payload handler's activate gets the installed payload (P4-16).

packs.provides.note: update.packs.provides reads the record-level provides (CONTENT_ID_PATTERN, MAX_PROVIDES; an unusable list provides nothing); client.update.packs.is_available over the running set and pack_for over a packs decision's targets or the stamp's pins, unentitled and revoked releases never answering.

packs.type.godot.zip.note: P4-16: a godot.zip is mounted only by Godot's load_resource_pack.

packs.type.l10n.table.note: P4-16: L10nTableHandler (built in): PO, CSV or JSON tables by content, plain parsers (never evaluated), each locale a well-formed BCP-47 tag matching the variant's locale axis; tables(pack_id), on_activate/on_deactivate.

packs.type.data.json.note: P4-16: DataJsonHandler (built in): every file one strict-JSON object (V4 §1.2), the format_versions the host lists; documents(pack_id), on_activate/on_deactivate.

packs.type.audio.bank.note: P4-16: audio banks load through a game engine's middleware.

packs.type.ml.model.note: P4-16: MlModelHandler (host-registered with runtimes, ram_bytes, vram_bytes, quantizations, load_test): model.json's runtime, quantisation and RAM/VRAM needs against the budget, then the load test, before model(pack_id) swaps.

packs.transport.steam.note: P5-08 covers Godot only; Python desktop hosts have no Steam-depot transport owner.

packs.transport.msix.note: No work package owns the MSIX optional-package transport (P5-08 Out).

packs.transport.flatpak.note: No work package owns the Flatpak extension transport (P5-08 Out).

Proofs: tests/cli/test_golden.py (golden ANSI in every variant and SVG for 70 component states in both themes), tests/cli/test_lint.py (catalog strings, 80/60 columns, piped output, RTL-safe source), tests/cli/test_flows.py (interactive flows with scripted keys, and rich's bytes against the kit's), tests/cli/test_responsive.py (the resolution matrix in pyte with soft-wrap marks and reflow: 40/60/80/120 columns at 12 and 24 rows with long values, de and ja at 40 and 60, and an 80 to 50 resize mid-flow by SIGWINCH; no line wider than the terminal, no URL or code cut, the code, URL and keys in view) and tests/cli/test_textual.py. The ui.gate … ui.i18n rows are UK-02b's and do not exist yet.

ui.cli.portal.note: polaris_key.core.portal (parse_portal, portal_link) over discovery's core.portal; Client.portal() holds the member and persists it as portal.json beside the presentation cache; the terminal kit draws portal_link() as the product page and Contact {developer} when it is None. commerce.receipt.note: polaris_key.commerce: binding() and claim(store, payload) over the P6-01 bridge, plus claim_steam(ticket_hex, dlc_app_id), claim_play() and claim_app_store(), which sync on success; the host's Steamworks binding supplies the ticket, so there is no store dependency. Refusals keep the server's code and reason (ClaimNotOwned, ClaimAttestationRequired, ClaimRefused). tests/test_commerce.py and the commerce-claim transcript.

sync.keyring.note: client.keyring (sdks/python/src/polaris_key/keyring/client.py) over polaris_key.core.sync_crypto on `cryptography` (HKDF, AES-256-GCM, X25519, HPKE mode_base written out): create(), unlock() (opens this device's wrap through the DeviceKeyPort's dh, so the agreement key never leaves the store), wrap_to()/remove_wrap(), set_recovery_code()/recover(), reset()/adopt()/open_adopted(), attach(machine) feeding set_root, and the codec. The root is held in memory only, never written, returned or shown in a repr, error or pickle; the host decides how a wrap travels (R-9). tests/test_keyring.py, tests/test_sync_crypto_conformance.py (sync-vectors.json: hkdf, envelope, blind, hpke anchor, wrap, recovery, adopt); the keyring-* transcripts replay in tests/test_transcripts.py.

connect.identity.note: polaris_key.core.peer_cert ports client-core's peer/cert.ts (verify_peer_cert, verify_ring, ring_expired, replace_ring, admit_peer) over the SDK's strict verify_jws; tests/test_connect_conformance.py runs peerCertCases, ringCases and peerAdmissionCases. client.connect (polaris_key/connect, CC-10.1): identity() registers the device keys on first need (a memory-only store refuses unless allow_ephemeral_keys), fetches GET connect/identity and verifies the roster and certificate against the effective set, refusing a stale, foreign, expired or other-keys answer with bad_response; the roster, certificate and K_disc are kept as pkey.connect.v1 (0600 in a 0700 state directory, never in a repr or log) with the previous K_disc dropped on a leave or key change and after 24 h; list_devices(), current(), discovery_keys(), leave(). tests/test_connect_identity.py. No identity transcript is recorded yet; the relay transcripts belong to connect.relay.

connect.noise.note: polaris_key.core.peer_noise: Noise_XX_25519_AESGCM_SHA256 on the cryptography package, a zero or failing DH refusing with dh_zero; tests/test_connect_noise.py replays noise-vectors.json.

connect.protocol.note: polaris_key.core peer codecs, frames, relay envelopes, SAS and the peer session (modes a, v, p; commit-reveal SAS, handshake limiter) and TrustManager.accept_peer; tests/test_connect_peer_*.py, test_connect_session.py and test_trust_accept_peer.py replay peer-matrix.json.

connect.lan.note: polaris_key.connect.lan and the bounded mDNS responder and browser (advert rotation, browse match, TCP listen and dial, G7 caps, wrong_peer, flood and write-buffer caps); tests/test_connect_lan.py, test_connect_mdns.py, test_connect_mdns_packet.py. IPv6 (CC-IPV6.4a, WIRE-CONTRACT-V5 §15.4): mDNS runs on 224.0.0.251 and on ff02::fb with one socket per interface (IPV6_JOIN_GROUP, IPV6_MULTICAST_IF; at most 8; the zone is the interface name; the interface list comes from getifaddrs through ctypes, and browsing raises MdnsUnavailableError where it cannot be read), the codec has AAAA, an advert's AAAA is the fe80 address the kernel sends from, a response from outside the receiving interface's connected subnets is ignored (RFC 6762 section 11), an A or AAAA record is learned only when equal to the packet source (the peer-matrix mdnsAnswers rows run in test_connect_peer_codecs.py), at most 4 addresses per name, and lan_verdict and lan_group_key (core/peer_lan_address.py, literal-only parsing, no ipaddress module) run the lanAddresses rows; the CANDIDATES rows are not run because this SDK neither sends nor reads that record (CC-08R). TCP (CC-IPV6.4b, §15.4.1): one dual-stack :: listener on one port (IPV6_V6ONLY off, 0.0.0.0 fallback); an accepted socket is judged by lan_verdict on its own peer and local address before a slot and before any read, a dialled address as text before the connect and on the connected socket before its first byte (connect/lan_judge.py); unauthenticated sockets are capped at 4 per address, 16 per /64 and 32 in total; a device with several addresses dials them in a 250 ms race with at most 2 in flight (connect/dial.py). tests/test_connect_lan.py runs it on ::1. Live multicast tests run only with PKEY_LIVE_MDNS=1.

connect.relay.note: client.connect.relay_ticket() and polaris_key.connect.relay (ticket offer, WebSocket socket via the optional websockets extra, reconnect policy, LIMIT and close codes, redirects refused, mode-a relay sessions, pacing, 8 MiB queue cap); tests/test_connect_relay*.py and test_connect_client_relay.py; tests/test_transcripts.py replays connect-relay-ticket and connect-relay-quota.

connect.app.note: client.cloud_connect (polaris_key.connect.cloud_connect): start, stop, peers, devices, open and on_channel, LAN then relay, the G21 off switches, G9 and the sign-out order, with an AsyncClient mirror; tests/test_cloud_connect.py.

server.license.note: polaris_key.server: PolarisKey (verdict, trust refresh, verified-document cache), with FastAPI/Starlette, Django/DRF and Flask adapters that import their framework lazily (extras starlette, fastapi, flask, django, drf). Replays backend-matrix.json's verdict and problem sections (tests/test_server_matrix.py) and gates a route in each framework. require_tier / require_all, get_polaris_license, CORS preflight pass, start-up config errors and polaris_key.server.testing: tests/test_server_dx.py.

server.signin.note: require_sign_in() / has_sign_in() read profile.user.subject through license_user; the verdict rows replay in tests/test_server_matrix.py.

server.config.note: server_client() (polaris_key.server_client): the normal client over an InMemoryStore pinned to PKEY_DEVICE_ID (or a 0600 file on a volume, PKEY_DEVICE_ID_FILE), the key from PKEY_LICENSE_KEY activated at start, device_reports=False (no devices/report, on sync or explicitly) and the refresh thread. tests/test_server_client.py.
